title: D Flip-Flop: One Bit of Memory at the Clock Edge
topic: D flip-flop — an edge-triggered storage cell whose output Q samples the input D at every rising edge of the clock; the cell behind every register and counter

beats.narration: A flip-flop remembers one bit — but only on command. What makes it latch?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
One bit of memory — but when does it remember?

beats.narration: Here's a D flip-flop — data in, clock in, and Q out. The triangle on the clock input means it's edge triggered.

elements.content: D flip-flop body — large rectangle
D label inside, left-aligned, near top input pin
Q label inside, right-aligned, near top output pin
CLK input pin (bottom-left) with a small triangle 'edge-triggered' marker inside the box
CLK label outside next to the clock pin
Three input/output stubs extending out from the rectangle
the triangle ▷ marks an edge-triggered input

beats.narration: Set up a clock signal toggling steadily, and a data signal moving in its own rhythm.

elements.content: Two stacked timing rows — CLK on top, D below
CLK: square wave with 4 cycles, traced in left-to-right
D: step pattern that changes at irregular intervals, traced in synchronously
the clock ticks. data wanders.

beats.narration: On every rising edge of the clock, Q samples whatever D is right then. Between edges, D can dance around freely and Q ignores it.

elements.content: Three stacked timing rows — CLK, D, Q — same time axis
CLK and D pre-shown; Q traces in as the time cursor sweeps left-to-right
Sample pulses at each rising clock edge — amber spark on CLK row, dashed verticals down to D and Q
elements.note: the genuine motion of this scene

elements.content: Live time cursor sweeping right; Q value step-updates each time it crosses a rising CLK edge to match D at that instant
Q catches D — but only on the clock's rising edge

beats.narration: Q catches D on the rising edge — that one bit of memory is the cell behind every register and counter.

elements.content: Q := D  on the rising edge of CLK
one bit, one edge — line up N of them and you have a register
stack registers on a shared clock and you have synchronous digital logic
